items.title: Hialeah Police arrest woman in death of goat seen in viral video
items.text:
Video showed the goat wandering through the streets of Hialeah with money attached to its body.

The NBC6 South Florida News streaming channel plays local South Florida news 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
A woman has been arrested in connection with the death of a goat that was captured on video wandering the streets of Hialeah with money attached to its body.
Alianne De La Caridad Trista, 34, was arrested two weeks after video of the goat went viral, Hialeah Police announced Friday.
The video circulated online on Oct. 30 and depicted the goat wandering loose with U.S. money attached to it. The animal was later struck and killed by a vehicle.
De La Caridad is now in custody, facing one count of aggravated animal cruelty resulting in death.
Hialeah Police thanked several agencies for their help, including ICE, the FBI, the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office and the Miami-Dade State Attorney’s Office.
"The Hialeah Police Department wants to make one message unmistakably clear to our community: We take acts of animal cruelty seriously, and we were never going to let this slide," police said. "Those who mistreat defenseless animals in our city will be held accountable."
items.desc: Video showed the goat wandering through the streets of Hialeah with money attached to its body.

items.title: Dolphins run game, run defense vital to success vs. Buffalo
items.text:
The Miami Dolphins visit Buffalo on Sunday, and running the ball and stopping the run will be the No. 1 goal to having a chance at victory.

MIAMI GARDENS — Two on-field traits represent what the rebuilding Dolphins are about as much as any others – running the ball and stopping the run.
Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks had a great description of the role that defensive tackles play for linebackers in run defense.
“They do everything,” Brooks said. “When you build a house, you’ve got to lay the foundation. The foundation, if it ain’t laid the right way, the house is going to eventually break down.”
That could be trouble this week as the Dolphins (1-8) , who are 16.5-point underdogs, visit Buffalo (8-1). The Dolphins , of course, are without three key defensive tackles this week — Zach Sieler (biceps), Jordan Phillips (biceps) and Zeek Biggers (knee).
Statistically speaking, the youthful, injury-challenged Dolphins are 17th in rushing offense at 113.1 yards per game and 18th in rushing defense at 118.4 ypg.
When Miami is on defense, the concern is that Buffalo’s rushing offense is led by rugged, versatile running back James Cook, the former Miami Central standout who is No. 2 in the league in rushing at 971 yards.
“This guy’s ability to make a cut in the backfield and just accelerate is really, really impressive,” defensive coordinator Sean Duggan said. “He’s really elusive when it comes to tackling. He’s got really good contact balance. He’s got a really good stiff arm.”
As a team, the Bills are No. 2 in rushing at 152.7 yards per game, and their offensive line, led by Dion Dawkins, the five-time Pro Bowl left tackle, is ranked No. 5 in the league by Pro Football Focus.
It’s hard to say stopping Buffalo’s run game is the most important aspect of the game, considering the Bills have All Pro quarterback Josh Allen. But stopping the Bills’ run game is vitally important.
The good news on that front is Miami’s run defense has been solid. Miami has fallen to No. 18 (118.4 ypg) and just allowed Indianapolis a season-high 172 yards rushing, but the Dolphins’ yards per carry (3.9) is tied for No. 7 in the league.

If Buffalo stacks the box, it will be incumbent on quarterback Kyle McCord to make good decisions and good throws to make the defense pay the price for committing so much attention to the run game, and perhaps that’s more likely if he utilizes the tight ends more this week than he did last week.
McCord didn’t throw deep a lot against the Colts, but he had the 38-yard completion to wide receiver Caleb Douglas among Douglas’ eight targets, many of which were on intermediate or deep routes.
On the other side of the ball, Buffalo, which will undoubtedly hit Miami with a slew of eight-man fronts designed to stop the run, are No. 8 in rushing defense at 93.6 yards per game.
Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II (539 yards rushing, four touchdowns) has been held to 69, 55 and 76 yards rushing in his past three games as defenses have stacked the box to prevent the run. The Dolphins have plunged to No. 17 in rushing offense (113.1 ypg) as they’ve been held to 74, 77 and 78 yards rushing the last three weeks.

items.title: The Real Miami Museums and Artists Behind GTA VI’s Vice City
items.text:
From The Bass in Miami Beach to the murals of Wynwood, the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI is heavily inspired by the local arts scene.

After 13 agonizing years of waiting for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), gamers worldwide wasted no time tearing up the streets of the game's fictional state of Leonida after it was released yesterday, November 19. The South Florida-inspired game environment is heavily influenced by the culture, environment, and architecture of Miami — from its Art Deco resorts, white-sand beaches, Cuban quarter, and strip clubs, right down to its museums and arts venues.
As fans embed themselves in GTA 6's immersive landscape, many have recognized real-life locations across South Florida making unexpected cameos. One such case is the Vice Museum of Art, which Rockstar Games confirmed is modeled after the Bass Museum of Art in Miami Beach.
“It was totally unexpected to see Grand Theft Auto VI reimagine The Bass as the ‘Vice City Museum of Art,’” said Silvia Karman Cubiñá, executive director of the Bass Museum of Art, in an email to Hyperallergic .
“It’s a wonderful reminder of how art and architecture can become part of popular culture,” she continued. “Now, I’m just curious: will the Vice City Museum of Art get more visitors than we do?!”
While not listed as a landmark like the Vice Museum of Art, another building in Downtown Vice City appears to be directly modeled after the Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM). Situated near the Vice City Arts Center , which is heavily based on Miami's Adrienne Arsht Center for Performing Arts, the PAMM-inspired building sits right on the water's edge just as the museum does in real life.
“We were as delighted as anyone else to find PAMM in what feels like the biggest video game of all time,” said Alexa Ferra, PAMM's senior director of marketing and communications, in an email to Hyperallergic.
Ferra attached a photo someone sent her from the game showing the PAMM dupe and some gummy bear-inspired sculptures installed in the shallow water.
“It's a testament to our stunning Herzog & de Meuron building, and goes to show if you stick around long enough, you'll pop up in the unlikeliest — but inevitable — of places.” Ferra added.
Other references to Miami's arts and culture scene include Leonida's Stockyard neighborhood, which directly channels the street murals and warehouse-lined roads of the Wynwood Arts District. It was reported earlier this summer that Rockstar Games had hired over 50 real street artists to design the in-game murals across Stockyard. Users shared they've spotted the works of street artist Ahol Sniffs Glue (David Anasagasti), among others.
Miami-raised contemporary photographer Josh Aronson also took notice of GTA 6's inclusion of his installation at the Catalina Hotel & Beach Club in Miami Beach during Miami Art Week 2024 , which Rockstar Games incorporated in Vice City's own Catalina Hotel. From Aronson's Florida Boys (2020–) photo series, the photo “Spring” (2024) was made into an enormous sublimated fabric print that hung from the second-story window of the hotel.
The same printed photo, which features a group of cheerful young men photographed from above while floating in water, is shown at Vice City's Catalina Hotel.
“Florida Boys is my own imagined version of Florida, so I love that it gets to live on in another imagined Florida,” Aronson told Hyperallergic . “The installation at the Catalina was temporary, but in Vice City, someone might stumble upon it years from now

items.title: Police officers investigate car submerged in Miami Beach canal
items.text: MIAMI BEACH, Fla. — One person was hospitalized after a car sank in a canal on Friday in Miami Beach, according to police. The car was in a canal shortly after 11:15 a.m., between Collins Avenue and Pine Tree Drive, just west of the Mid-Beach neighborhood. The sole occupant of the car managed to get out and swim to safety near 46th Avenue, according to Officer Christopher Bess, a spokesman for the Miami Beach Police Department. Miami Beach Fire Rescue personnel took the person, whose condition was stable, to the Mount Sinai Medical Center as a “precaution,” according to Bess. Detectives asked anyone with information about this or other cases to call Miami-Dade County Crime Stoppers at 305-471-8477 to remain anonymous. Local 10 News Assignment Desk Manager Kelly Davis contributed to this report. Location
items.desc: One person was hospitalized after a car sank in a canal on Friday in Miami Beach, according to police.

items.title: Troubled tow company owner heard in Miami-Dade jail calls plotting more fraud from behind bars: Cops
items.text: MIAMI — Not even being locked up could stop a troubled Miami-Dade tow company owner from committing fraud, deputies say: He was heard in recorded jail calls encouraging an employee to rip off rental companies, they say. Leer en español Now, ASAP Towing owner Oscar Rodriguez, who already has an extensive criminal history in the county ― and pending cases ― is facing an additional two first-degree felonies. Local 10 News has previously reported on another case involving ASAP Towing, based at 2154 NW 95th St. in the unincorporated West Little River area. State records show the 37-year-old Rodriguez, also known as “Pipo,” is currently serving a five-year probation term on a host of charges, including grand theft, running a chop shop and vehicle title fraud. He also briefly spent time in state prison in 2015 on theft, burglary and cocaine charges. But it’s his time in the Miami-Dade jail, followed an arrest this summer, that’s leading to his latest case. Rodriguez has been locked up since July for what deputies said was his illegal use of a county-owned vacant lot to store towed vehicles and presenting what officials said was a fraudulent lease agreement. While behind bars, deputies said Rodriguez was heard in jail calls telling his manager to scam vehicle rental companies. “During one conversation, (Rodriguez) instructed (him) on how to make a vehicle appear to have sustained water damage. (The) asked whether he should soak the vehicle to make it appear flooded and justify charging for additional labor,” the report states. “On another occasion, (Rodriguez) is heard advising (his manager) to charge rental companies extra, due to them (being) willing to pay whatever to have their vehicles released.” ASAP Towing overcharged rental companies more than $123,000 over the span of a year, deputies said. In one instance, Rodriguez is accused of stealing a BMW X1 from rental company Sixt. According to an arrest report, Sixt tried have another company get the vehicle back from the ASAP lot, but deputies said “refused to release it and (falsely) advised that a police hold had to be lifted.” Rodriguez was eventually busted driving the vehicle in Hialeah, earning him an auto theft charge, deputies said. Deputies added new grand theft and organized fraud charges from the case on Thursday, while Rodriguez was already locked up in the county’s Pre-Trial Detention Center near the criminal courthouse in Miami. Records show he remained at the PTDC as of Friday. His online jail card reads more like a CVS receipt, with more than two dozen charges stacked across various cases and warrants, including counts of theft, running a chop shop and title fraud.

items.title: Miami-Dade schools to resume operations Friday following South Florida flooding
items.text:
Miami-Dade County Public Schools (M-DCPS) will resume normal operations Friday, Nov. 20, following heavy rainfall and flooding that disrupted activities across South Florida this week.
Superintendent Rafael A. Villalobos announced Thursday that all public schools, region offices, district offices and school-related activities will operate as scheduled Friday.
The announcement comes as South Florida continues to recover from a period of heavy rainfall that prompted flooding concerns, road closures and disruptions to government services in parts of the region.
Unlike neighboring Broward County, where public schools will remain closed Friday because of ongoing flooding, Miami-Dade students and employees are expected to return to their regular schedules.
The district had canceled classes Thursday, Nov. 19, including adult education, after-school care, athletic events and other school activities, because of severe weather conditions. Region and district offices were also closed.
The decision to reopen followed assessments of schools and facilities by district officials. M-DCPS said it would continue sharing updates as needed.
Meanwhile, Broward County Public Schools announced that its schools and district offices would remain closed Friday. Broward students are not expected to return to classrooms until Monday, Nov. 30, following the Thanksgiving break, while district offices are expected to reopen Monday, Nov. 23.
Florida International University also announced plans to resume classes and normal operations Friday, although officials cautioned that some roads could remain affected by localized flooding.
Families can monitor the M-DCPS website and the district's official social media accounts for additional announcements
